OMEGA-05/11: experiences that resist scoring, and the firewall before value

Two organs the North Star names and nothing implemented.

experience-compiler.mjs. The obvious version of this module is a scoring
function over experiences, and the obvious version is the failure: a
system that ranks a life by expected value recommends against rest,
against play, against the unrepeatable thing that produces no measurable
gain, and is internally correct every time. So three things sit outside
the arithmetic rather than inside it as penalty terms -- a penalty term
can always be outweighed by a large enough number somewhere else.
An experience whose whole value is being had leaves the ranking entirely
rather than scoring zero. An age-, person- or moment-bound experience is
set apart rather than given a bonus. A declared off-limits domain stays
unmodelled however useful modelling it would be, and the usefulness is
recorded precisely so it can be seen not to have won.

Compound value counts dimensions rather than summing them, because a sum
erases the difference between a little of six things and a lot of one --
the difference the compiler exists to surface. The module ships no
weighting: a weight vector is a claim about what matters, and one shipped
in a module would be the imposed worldview the canon forbids.

ruin-firewall.mjs. Expected value gets ruin wrong in a specific way: it
averages over paths, and ruin is the path where there are no further
paths. A bet with excellent expected value and a 3% chance of ending the
game is not a good bet made 33 times. So this screens before any scoring
and no number clears an absorbing outcome -- a firewall rather than a
penalty, and with no probability threshold, because a threshold is a
number someone tunes downward under pressure and the tuning always
happens on the option somebody already wants. An unclassified outcome
blocks the screen rather than passing as safe: the unclassified one is
usually the novel one, which is exactly what has no label yet and exactly
what matters. A recovery plan without a detection step is refused,
because nothing starts the clock. correlatedExposure reports effective
independent positions, since five sharing one dependency are one.

Both are wired into api/sovereign-control.mjs, so they have a caller. The
ruin screen is reported alongside the decision packet and never folded
into the ranking -- an option that can end the ability to choose again is
not a low-scoring option, it is a different kind of thing, and the test
pins that the 97%-good bet still wins the ranking while failing the
screen.

sovereignty-type-system.mjs (OMEGA-04) is the spine. UberBond's

promotion: an observation becomes a belief, a belief a prediction, a
prediction arrives worded as a command, and the command runs because it
sounded confident. Every step reads fine in a log. Three edges on the
ladder are human acts rather than inferences -- is->ought,
recommendation->choice, choice->authority -- and rung-skipping is refused

rung governs a derivation, so one value judgment cannot hide inside nine
facts. Delegation must originate with the founder, name the action and
expire; re-delegation may only attenuate and may not outlive its parent
-- the failure that is actually hard to see is a chain where every hop
narrows the action set while the expiry walks forward.

look identical from outside because both end in a confident answer:
a universe that was five wordings of one option, and a probability with
nothing under it. Options merge on a causal signature, so the merge count
exposes a generator producing variants. A probability requires
quantitative evidence -- a causal model says how, not how often -- and
correlated sources count once, because ten models sharing a corpus are
one observation repeated. The packet stops at RECOMMENDATION and declines
to name a winner when the remaining difference is a value choice.

The exact denominator, computed rather than asserted: 1068 concepts extracted
from ten canonical sources, 1038 rows, 30 alias merges, zero dropped.

UberBond's recurring failure has never been losing code. It has been losing
concepts -- an idea named once, donated by a superseded program, or buried in a
list of 170, quietly falling out of the project's own account of itself. So the
compiler refuses to emit a matrix whose row count does not equal its input
count, and every row's state is computed from repository evidence.

Getting the evidence honest took three corrections, each in a different
direction:

- **It indexed only src/.** Mutation War is a scripts/ module with seven suites
  and a mutation registry behind it, and it was reporting SPEC_ONLY -- an idea
  nobody had built. scripts/ and api/ are implementation surfaces and are now
  indexed.
- **Compound names matched nothing.** Canon names a concept and its qualifier in
  one string ("Mutation War and independent verification"), and requiring every
  word found nothing. Names now split on explicit conjunctions.
- **That split is also how this becomes a fiction.** "GENESIS for Life" contains
  "GENESIS", and scoring it off that would invent a Personal Civilization organ
  out of an unrelated frontier engine. So names are never split on whitespace,
  and a part-match is recorded as SUB_PHRASE and capped at PARTIAL_CURRENT --
  part of a concept existing is a different fact from the concept existing.

Verified in both directions: Mutation War, Capability Genome and Wallbreaker
find their evidence; every "for Life" variant correctly stays SPEC_ONLY.

The matcher's conservative bias is recorded in the artifact itself, because
SPEC_ONLY must not be read as a finding. "Event Horizon capital allocation"
reads SPEC_ONLY while src/event-horizon.mjs exists. An under-claimed row is a
lead for a human; an over-claimed one is a lie that compounds.
